source_policy: Official SBC sources only: the Baptist Faith and Message 2000 as amended (bfm.sbc.net) and the SBC Constitution (sbc.net).

nuance.title: Autonomy and cooperation
paragraphs: Every Southern Baptist church is autonomous. The Convention states it claims no authority over any church, so nothing it adopts binds a congregation.

Cooperation is a different matter. The SBC Constitution counts a church as cooperating only when its faith and practice closely identify with the Baptist Faith and Message, and it names affirming homosexual behavior as one example of a church that is not in cooperation.
The Baptist Faith and Message limits the office of pastor/elder/overseer to men. A given church's own practice still decides its own rating; check the church's page.

rule.text: The official confession affirms Scripture is without error (inerrant) and the final authority (also worded "supreme standard", "ultimate authority" or "only infallible rule of faith and practice") → GREEN. Both halves need a quote.
The official confession affirms Christ is fully God and fully man (also worded "truly God and truly man" or "very God and very man") → GREEN.
An official decision or confession restricts ordination or the pastoral office to qualified men → GREEN. Non-ordained ministry roles for women are noted, not penalized.

The official confession affirms justification by grace through faith alone in Christ alone (also worded "justified by faith only", not by works, or justification defined as God's gracious acquittal of sinners who repent and believe in Christ) → GREEN.

preaching.note: No validated official quote maps to a published rule.

rule.text: An official statement defines marriage as one man and one woman → GREEN.
The official confession limits the pastor/elder office to men → GREEN. Where the body is autonomous, each church's own evidence still decides.
The official mission is gospel or church multiplication among all people → GREEN.

mens_discipleship.note: No validated official quote maps to a published rule.

rule.text: Not on the published LGBTQ-affirming list, and an official statement defines marriage as one man and one woman → GREEN.
Each church is autonomous and the body disclaims any authority over it; its confession binds no church. Cooperation or affiliation can still require agreement with that confession → AUTONOMOUS.

ledger.quote: It has God for its author, salvation for its end, and truth, without any mixture of error, for its matter.

It reveals the principles by which God judges us, and therefore is, and will remain to the end of the world, the true center of Christian union, and the supreme standard by which all human conduct, creeds, and religious opinions should be tried.
He ascended into heaven and is now exalted at the right hand of God where He is the One Mediator, fully God, fully man, in whose Person is effected the reconciliation between God and man.
Justification is God’s gracious and full acquittal upon principles of His righteousness of all sinners who repent and believe in Christ.
There is no salvation apart from personal faith in Jesus Christ as Lord.
While both men and women are gifted for service in the church, the office of pastor/elder/overseer is limited to men as qualified by Scripture.
Marriage is the uniting of one man and one woman in covenant commitment for a lifetime.
In the spirit of Christ, Christians should oppose racism, every form of greed, selfishness, and vice, and all forms of sexual immorality, including adultery, homosexuality, and pornography.
(By way of example, churches which act to affirm, approve, or endorse homosexual behavior would be deemed not to be in cooperation with the Convention.)
It is the duty and privilege of every follower of Christ and of every church of the Lord Jesus Christ to endeavor to make disciples of all nations.
A New Testament church of the Lord Jesus Christ is an autonomous local congregation of baptized believers
While independent and sovereign in its own sphere, the Convention does not claim and will never attempt to exercise any authority over any other Baptist body
